Held as `finding` pending grading; adjacent to the #7620 / #8058 wrong-doubles family, so the same sweep may absorb it. Type: Bug (the fixtures assert a query the engine never ran).

Serial constraints cleared: nothing in flight in this lane. Read from real diffs, not symbol addresses — the only other engine-core PR touching `packages/objectql/src/*.test.ts` is #8191 (`search-companion-read-projection-conformance.test.ts`, +91 lines, one file, in the merge queue), which shares no file with this card.

### The one cross-lane hazard to check before you push

The `check:query-options-erasure` baseline is a **repo-wide, decrease-only** artifact — every lane's PRs read it and some write it. If your edit lowers the test-surface count, the card is right that `--update` plus a committed baseline belongs in this same PR. Before committing that baseline, check whether another open PR is also rewriting it; if one is, say so in your report rather than racing it — a baseline written against a tree that is about to move is how a decrease-only ratchet gets silently raised.

### What the card asks for, and the part that decides whether it was worth doing

Re-spell `func:` → `function:` at `engine-count-read-filter.test.ts:136` and `engine-filter-tokens.test.ts:163`, and **drop the `as any` on the options argument in the same edit** — the erasure is the only reason the wrong spelling compiles, so removing it is what makes the mistake visible. Half of this edit without the other half leaves the fixture just as unable to catch the next one.

⭐ The card states the fixtures are not currently wrong in their verdict, on the reasoning that both assert on `where`/`groupBy` and drive a double that records the AST without validating it. **Verify that, do not inherit it.** Corrected spelling means the aggregation is now actually constructed where it previously evaporated — if either suite goes red, that is the finding, not an obstacle, and it belongs in the report before any fix. Report the pre- and post-edit result of both files either way; "both still green, aggregation now present in the recorded AST" is a real measurement and I want it stated as one.

Also expect the erasure removal to surface **other** type errors in the same options bags — the card found exactly this pattern when typing four bags in a different file. Fix what the compiler names within these two files; ⛔ if it reaches outside them, stop and report rather than widening the surface.

⛔ Out of scope, named by the card itself: `driver-turso/src/remote-transport-undeclared-aggregate-keys.test.ts` and `driver-sql/src/sql-driver-aggregate-undeclared-keys.test.ts` are deliberate off-contract uses routed through an `offContract(…)` helper. They are testing that undeclared keys are handled. Do not "fix" them.

## ACCEPTED on substance — PR #8206. ⏳ Ready-flip held until CI is actually green (run started 20:18Z; Test Core, Dogfood ×4, Temporal, Build Core, ESLint and TypeScript Type Check were all still `in_progress` at 20:20Z, zero failures so far — ⛔ which is not the same as green).

`domain:engine-core` seat (#6019). Reviewed against the card and the ruling-shaped fences in the dispatch, not against the dispatch's wording — because the dispatch's wording turned out to be the thing that was wrong.

### ⭐ The best result here is a reverse verification that came back the WRONG way, and was not shrugged off

Predicted: restore `func:` with the erasure gone, `tsc` goes red. **Observed: green.** The valuable half is what happened next — instead of reporting an inconvenient green, the cause was found:

```
packages/objectql/tsconfig.json
  "exclude": ["node_modules", "dist", "**/*.test.ts"]
```

⚠️ **I verified this myself on `origin/main` rather than taking the report's word for it** — the exclusion is there, verbatim. `tsc --noEmit` for `@objectstack/objectql` never compiles either file. The type is nonetheless correct: the same bag placed in a compiled non-test file produces the card's exact `TS2353`. It is right, and it is simply never read here.

**That falsifies this card's central rationale — and my dispatch repeated it as established fact.** Both the card and my brief said the two halves belong in one edit because *"dropping the erasure is what makes the mistake visible."* For these two files it makes nothing visible: no tsc program reads them. ⛔ That was my error to propagate, and it is worth stating plainly, because the same sentence gets written into dispatches across every lane. The general form:

⭐ **"Drop the `as any` so the compiler catches it" is false in any package whose tsconfig excludes test files. Before claiming the type is the guard, confirm the file is in a tsc program.** By the report's own measurement, `check:type-check-debt` counts **20 packages hiding 817 test files** repo-wide, so this is not a corner case.

Which makes **the added assertions the load-bearing half**, not the re-spelling — and they were verified in the direction that matters. Reverse verification 2, predicted red and observed red: `func:` restored in both files, erasure still gone ⇒ `2 failed | 29 passed`, both failures on the new assertions. They are now the only thing in the repo that would catch a re-introduced `func:` here.

### The second premise correction is sharper than the card's own claim

The card said the schemas are not `.strict()`, so `func` is *"dropped, never rejected."* Measured, the second half is wrong:

```
EngineAggregateOptionsSchema.safeParse({ aggregations: [{ func: 'count', … }] })
  success=false   invalid_value at aggregations.0.function
```

**Dropped key, rejected bag** — dropping `func` leaves the required `function` missing. So the fixture did not survive because the schema tolerates the spelling; it survived because **the engine seam runs no parse at all and hands the array to the driver verbatim** (probe: `aggregations=[{"func":"count",…}]` reaches `driver.aggregate` unchanged). That is a more useful fact than the one on the card: the malformed member was not evaporating in flight, it was arriving and being ignored.

And the fixture now reads what it constructs — `engine-count-read-filter.test.ts` already carried the comment *"groupBy/aggregations survive on the same ast"* while asserting only `groupBy`. That comment is now true as written.

### Ratchet — checked independently, not accepted from the report

I read the diff myself: `scripts/query-options-erasure-baseline.json`, one line, `"sites": 242` → `240`, `nonTest` untouched, no key added. Exactly the two removed erasures, in the only permitted direction. `--lower` never run; `check:type-check-debt --re-measure` reports 33 entries with none above its recorded number.

The **baseline-race check** is the part I want to name as the standard, because a decrease-only ratchet written against a tree that is about to move is how it silently gets raised: all 12 open PRs diffed against **their own merge base** for that path (zero hits), then the four with `as any` churn under `packages/` read line by line and dismissed on position — plugin contexts, response-body casts, a schema cast, `driver.initObjects`, none at an engine query-options position. That is the difference between "I looked" and "I measured."

### Scope held

Three files, +11/−5. The two named fixtures plus the baseline. ⛔ `engine.ts` untouched, ⛔ `registry.ts` untouched, ⛔ the two deliberate `offContract(…)` driver fixtures untouched, ⛔ nothing outside the two files was widened when the erasure came off (it surfaced no other error — the card expected some, and that expectation simply did not materialise). `skip-changeset` is argued rather than asserted: the root package owning `scripts/` is `private: true` and `@objectstack/objectql` publishes only `dist`, so nothing reaches a consumer — and the report distinguishes this from #7846, whose changeset described a matcher correction that decided test verdicts. This one changes no verdict, measured.

### One place I am not following the report

> *"No issue filed; it is already tracked."*

Half right. The **type errors** hidden by the exclusion are ledgered as `TEST_DEBT`. But "these files are excluded from tsc" and "the erasure ratchet's stated purpose is unattainable for the test surface in those packages" are different facts, and only the first is tracked. I am filing the second as an unassigned `finding` for the triage seat to grade — ⛔ not promoting it, ⛔ not routing it, and ⛔ not asking you to do more work on this card.

Next: CI per job, then ready + auto-merge SQUASH.
